meta.description: Title formula library derived from competitive analysis of 8 top faceless geopolitical/economics channels

thumbnail_system.name: Yin-Yang Thumbnail Text
rules: Must be readable at mobile thumbnail size
Should trigger an emotional reaction BEFORE the viewer reads the title
If the title is analytical, the thumbnail is emotional
If the title is emotional, the thumbnail is specific
Thumbnail text and title must be DIFFERENT but complementary

title_thumbnail_pairing.rule: Title and thumbnail text must cover different parts of the curiosity gap. Title carries the 'what' and 'who'. Thumbnail text carries the emotional reaction or consequence.

examples.title: Why Germany Is Quietly Falling Apart
How Saudi Arabia Is Secretly Reshaping Global Finance
Something Strange Is Happening to China's Economy

master_formulas.name: Hidden Mechanism Exposé
master_formulas.psychology: Names villain + implies wrongdoing + specific 'how' creates irresistible curiosity gap
master_formulas.best_for: Corporate power plays, government manipulation, financial engineering
examples: How the Ultra Wealthy Evade Taxes with Fine Art
How BlackRock Quietly Bought Every Government on Earth
How Saudi Arabia Is Secretly Reshaping Global Finance

master_formulas.name: Causal Authority ('Why' Opener)
master_formulas.psychology: Promises causal explanation, not just facts. Viewer will UNDERSTAND something.
master_formulas.best_for: Country-level analysis, structural economic problems, geopolitical positioning
examples: Why Russia Thinks It Needs To Restore The Old Soviet Borders
Why Argentina Is Doomed To Fail Over and Over Again
Why Middle Class Americans Can't Afford Anything

master_formulas.name: Vague Alarm + Location
master_formulas.psychology: Maximum curiosity from vagueness of 'something' + grounding specificity of location
master_formulas.best_for: Breaking/emerging economic shifts, country-level crises, paradigm changes
examples: Something Weird Is Happening In Japan
Something Terrible Is Happening in Italy
Something Weird is Happening in California
power_doctrine_adaptations: Something [Adjective] Is Happening in [Country] (And Nobody's Talking About It)

master_formulas.name: Superlative Drama Noun
master_formulas.psychology: Mini-movie title card effect. Superlatives signal definitive, deep-dive content.
master_formulas.best_for: Corporate scandals, historical parallels, institutional failures
examples: Enron - The Biggest Fraud in History
Builder.ai - The Greatest AI Scam in History
Theranos: The Most Evil Business In The World

master_formulas.name: Worse Than You Thought
master_formulas.psychology: Direct second-person address + implication viewer's understanding is dangerously incomplete
master_formulas.best_for: Tech platforms, economic crises, geopolitical threats viewers already know about
examples: TikTok Is Worse Than You Thought
The FTX Disaster is Deeper Than you Think
The Metaverse Is Worse Than You Thought
power_doctrine_adaptations: The [Known Event] Is [Deeper] Than Anyone Realizes

master_formulas.name: Ominous Possessive Decline
master_formulas.psychology: Compact, authoritative. Possessive signals deep-dive specificity. Adjective adds emotional dimension.
master_formulas.best_for: Slow-burn economic decline, structural weakness stories, country profiles
examples: Australia's Quiet Collapse
China's Crumbling Economic Story
Germany's Unexpected Economic Crisis

master_formulas.name: Parenthetical Stakes Escalation
master_formulas.psychology: CaspianReport innovation. Main clause hooks, parenthetical escalates stakes and adds personal relevance.
master_formulas.best_for: Geopolitical cascading effects, connecting distant events to viewer's life
examples: Pakistan is dying (and that is a global problem)
America is already at war with Venezuela (open war is next)
The dollar is losing power (and your savings are exposed)
power_doctrine_adaptations: [System] is [failing] (and [who] is already positioning for what comes next)

scoring_rules.description: Score each title candidate 0-100 using these weighted criteria

criteria.name: proper_noun_present
criteria.rule: Title MUST contain at least one proper noun (country, company, institution, person). No proper noun = automatic 0 score.
criteria.rationale: Across all 8 channels, specificity of entity is the strongest predictor of views. Vague subjects kill performance.

criteria.name: emotional_stakes_clear
criteria.rule: Stakes must be immediately obvious within first 50 characters. Words like 'collapse', 'trap', 'crisis', 'secretly' signal stakes.
criteria.rationale: Titles that telegraph consequences outperform those that merely describe topics.

criteria.name: curiosity_gap_calibrated
criteria.rule: Title promises something specific the viewer doesn't know but wants to. Gap must be between what viewer currently knows and what title promises.
criteria.rationale: Too vague = no click. Too specific = no need to click. The gap must be answerable but surprising.

criteria.name: front_loaded_hook
criteria.rule: Primary entity name and emotional hook must appear in first 50 characters (mobile truncation point).
criteria.rationale: Mobile truncation occurs at 45-50 characters. The hook must survive truncation.

criteria.name: negative_framing
criteria.rule: Negative framing outperforms positive by 63%. Prefer crisis/threat/decline language over opportunity/growth.
criteria.rationale: Outbrain study of 65,000 headlines. Amplified in geopolitics niche where viewers are threat-aware.

criteria.name: power_doctrine_alignment
criteria.rule: Title should imply a hidden strategy, playbook, or power dynamic being revealed. Bonus for framework references (Thucydides Trap, Machiavellian, etc.)
criteria.rationale: Channel brand differentiation. 'There's ALWAYS a hidden playbook operating.'

hard_rules: Total length: 50-90 characters (sweet spot for CTR + mobile visibility)
NEVER use all-caps for entire title (1-2 words max for emphasis)
ALWAYS include a proper noun — no exceptions
Front-load the entity: first 50 chars must contain the main subject
Prefer 'Why' as opener when the video explains causation
Use numbers/dollar amounts when available (15-25% CTR boost)
Thumbnail text must be DIFFERENT from title (yin-yang system)
